extracted.intended_audience: Commenters and stakeholders in the FAA UAS BVLOS rulemaking (UAS operators, manufacturers, standards organizations, attorneys, tribes, and federal agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Official FAA Federal Register notice explaining the denial of a request to extend a reopened comment period for the BVLOS UAS NPRM, laying out the agency's procedural standards, factual findings, and legal bases for granting or denying extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of reopened comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: FAA finds that 14 days is sufficient to obtain comment on the limited topics described in the January 28, 2026, notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sufficiency by considering the scope of the reopened notice (narrow, limited topics) and prior opportunities for comment; a short reopened period can be adequate when the issues were already addressed in the original NPRM and existing comment volume is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior comment opportunities and existing record
rubrics_metrics.description: The topics were already broached in the NPRM and during the initial 60-day comment period, during which FAA received approximately 3,100 comments on the totality of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating extension requests, weigh whether commenters already had a substantive opportunity to comment (initial comment period length and content), and whether the existing comments substantially cover the reopened topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity of topics does not automatically justify extension
rubrics_metrics.description: While the topics of the questions are complex, FAA asserts that the reopened comment period provides sufficient opportunity for interested persons to provide feedback on the limited topics given they are topics that were already broached in the NPRM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must show why complexity prevents meaningful comment within the reopened timeframe; complexity alone is insufficient if prior notice and comment occurred on the same subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated impact of external events (e.g., lapse in funding) on ability to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: FAA disagrees that a lapse in funding impacting the Department of Transportation has interrupted the reopened comment period, stating the lapse does not impact the ability for commenters to review the NPRM or submit comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To succeed, an extension request based on external events must demonstrate that the event actually prevents commenters (or agencies) from accessing materials or submitting comments; speculative or indirect impacts are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency commenting opportunities via OIRA do not require extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Other federal agencies have the opportunity to review the final rule and provide comments during the interagency coordination process handled by the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs pursuant to E.O. 12866, a process independent of the notice and comment process under the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests claiming federal agencies will be prejudiced by lack of time to comment should account for OIRA interagency review as an alternative channel; that process can satisfy agency involvement without extending public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of prejudice from extension (delay harms stakeholders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping the reopened comment period open for an extended period on these limited topics could delay finalizing this rule. This delay would negatively impact other stakeholders, including UAS operators, manufacturers, standards organizations, and providers of supporting third-party services as they rely on the finalization of this rule to build and scale their operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding whether to extend, weigh potential harms from delay to affected stakeholders and the public interest in timely finalization; preventing undue delay is a legitimate ground to deny extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of reopened comment solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice asks seven questions to solicit comments limited to electronic conspicuity and right-of-way to ensure FAA fully understands these comments and the relevant policy implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopened comment periods may be narrowly scoped; comments should be limited to the specified topics. Extension requests should demonstrate a need for broader or longer solicitation only if the scope or complexity warrants it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on requester to show extension is in the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The commenter requested extension 'until February 28, 2026, or such time thereafter as the Administrator deems appropriate is in the public interest.' FAA considered and denied the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request framed as being 'in the public interest' must provide concrete reasons and evidence why additional time would materially improve the rulemaking record and serve public interests; conclusory assertions are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statutory and regulatory authorities to support procedural decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision issued under authority provided by 49 U.S.C. 106(f) and 44701, with reference to 5 U.S.C. 553(c) (summary of notice and comment rulemaking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency decisions on comment periods and extensions should be grounded in statutory/regulatory authority; cite controlling authorities and applicable executive order processes when explaining procedural determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of stakeholder reliance on regulatory finalization timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: FAA notes that stakeholders rely on the finalization of this rule to build and scale their operations, and that extended comment periods could delay those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider stakeholder reliance and concrete downstream effects (investment, operational planning, standards development) when deciding whether additional comment time is justified.
